Map tiles and data from OpenStreetMap and others carry licence terms that require visible credit. Hiding it breaches the licence.
Keep the attribution control visible and linked on every map.
Remove the attribution to tidy the corner.
Give a Text Alternative to the Map
A map image is invisible to a screen reader. The address, directions and key points should also exist as text.
Print the address and a short route description beside the map.
Present a location only as an embedded map.
Panning and zooming by drag excludes keyboard and switch users. Arrow keys and zoom buttons must work.
Enable keyboard handlers and visible zoom controls.
Do Not Use Colour Alone on Maps
Red and green pins cannot be told apart by many users. Differ by shape, label or icon.
Vary marker shape or add short labels.
Use only hue to encode categories.
Counts per region follow population, so a big region always looks worst. Use rates or per-capita figures.
Map rates per 1,000 people, and state the base in the legend.
Rainbow scales distort perceived differences. Sequential single-hue or ColorBrewer ramps read correctly and are safer for colour blindness.
Use sequential ramps for ordered data and diverging for a midpoint.
Popups that insert user text as HTML allow script injection. Set text, not markup.
Build popup content with textContent or sanitise first.
Hundreds of overlapping markers freeze phones and hide each other. Clusters expand on zoom.
Group points beyond a density threshold into clusters.
Pushing a 50 MB GeoJSON to the browser is slow. Tiles send only what the viewport needs.
Serve large layers as vector tiles.
Fly-to animations over long distances can trigger dizziness. Jump or fade when reduced motion is set.
People must know when text or images come from a model, and that it may be wrong.
Label generated content and add a short reliability note near it.
Present generated text as human or authoritative.
Stream Responses With a Stop Control
Streaming shows progress, but a stream that cannot be stopped traps users. Announce completion politely.
Show a stop button and set aria-live='polite' on a finished-message region.
Stream with no way to cancel.
A thumbs rating with an optional reason improves quality and signals that the system can be wrong.
Offer a quick rating and a free-text reason.
Users should be able to correct their prompt, regenerate and undo applied changes.
Provide edit, retry and revert for each result.
Eye-and-pinch input is less precise than a mouse. Targets need to be large with clear hover feedback.
Use at least 60pt targets and highlight on gaze.
Too many depth layers cause eye strain. Keep key content on one plane and use depth for hierarchy.
Limit depth to two or three layers and keep text on a flat plane.
Password managers need the right autocomplete tokens and standard fields. Breaking them pushes people to weak, reused passwords.
Use autocomplete='current-password' and 'new-password' and a normal form.
Randomise field names or block autofill.
Mask Sensitive Values With a Reveal
Card numbers and tokens shown in full are visible to shoulder surfers. Mask by default and let the user reveal.
Show the last four digits and a reveal control.
Sudden sign-out on a form wastes work. Warn before, and return people to where they were afterwards.
Show a countdown prompt and keep state through re-login.
Redirect silently to the login page.
Suggestions need combobox semantics so screen readers can hear options and arrow keys can pick them.
Follow the ARIA combobox pattern with aria-activedescendant.
Show a plain list of divs.
'0 results' is a dead end. Suggest spelling fixes, broader terms or popular items.
Say what was searched, offer alternatives and a contact route.
No matches for 'boilr'. Try 'boiler' or call us.
On sites with many pages, search should be one click away in a consistent place, inside a search landmark.
Use role='search' with a labelled input.
Forced tours annoy returning users. Allow skip and make help reachable again.
Provide Skip and a 'Show tips' option in settings.
Block use until a tour finishes.
Ask Only What You Need Now
Long sign-ups cause drop-off. Ask for the minimum, and collect extras once the value is clear.
Request email first, add profile fields later.
Bulk Actions Are Reversible and Counted
Selecting many rows and applying an action is risky. Show the count and allow undo.
Display '12 selected' and confirm with the number.
A column header that sorts needs a button inside and aria-sort for state.
Put a button in th and set aria-sort.
A calendar-only picker is slow for birth dates and tiring for keyboard users. Let people type the date.
Accept typed dates with a clear format and show a calendar as an extra.
Phone Number Is a Tap-to-call Link
Most local customers phone from a phone. A tel: link turns the number into one tap, and it can sit in the header.
Wrap the number in a tel: link with the international format.
Print the number as plain text or an image.
Visitors want to know if you are open now. Hours in plain text with today's status save a call.
List hours in text, and say 'Open until 5pm' using the visitor's date.
Put hours in an image or only in a footer.
A visitor with a van or a car needs directions in one tap. The address as text plus a maps link covers both.
Write the full address in text and link it to a maps URL.
Show only an embedded map with no text.
One Clear Action Above the Fold
A visitor deciding whether to call or book should see the one action straight away, in the first screen on a phone.
Place one primary button or phone link in the hero and repeat it in the header.
People hesitate when they cannot guess a cost. 'From' prices or typical ranges set expectations.
State 'from' prices or a range and what affects them.
Accreditations, insurance and review counts should be checkable. Link to the register or review page.
Link each badge to its public register entry.
Quote and Booking Forms Stay Short
Quote forms with ten fields lose phone users. Ask for name, contact and the job, then follow up.
Limit the first form to about four fields and a text box.
Ask for budgets, ratings and company size up front.
Avoid Gradient Text and Gradient Buttons
Gradient fills on headings and primary buttons are a leading tell of generic design and often reduce contrast at the edges.
Use one flat colour from the palette for text and actions.
Cards inside cards, or borders around every block, flatten hierarchy and look templated.
Separate groups with space and one container level.
Wrap each block in a bordered rounded card.
Skip the Eyebrow on Every Heading
A tiny uppercase label above every section title repeats and adds noise; use one only where it adds meaning.
Write a clear heading; add a label only when it names a category.
Put a small caps label above each h2.
Icon Cards Are Not a Layout
Three identical icon cards in a row say little. Content of unequal weight should look unequal.
Pick one main point and give it room; support with plain text.
Repeat icon, title, blurb three times.
A hero with a generic gradient or stock figure says nothing about the business. A photo of the work, product or place does.
Use an original photo of the work, or type alone.
Use abstract blobs or stock laptop images.
Custom players often lose keyboard support. Native controls provide it by default.
Use the native controls attribute or follow a tested player.
Hide controls and use a click-only overlay.
A chart image or canvas is opaque to assistive tech. Offer a summary and the data in a table.
Add a short text summary and a data table.
Ship a chart as a bare image.
Maps, videos and widgets pop in and push content down. A fixed aspect ratio box prevents it.
Wrap embeds in a box with aspect-ratio.
